title: Add scope to `rspm create token` command
description:
When trying to [generate an API token](https://github.com/rstudio/package-manager-demo/blob/main/r-package-manager-demo/README.md#api-token-generation) an error `Error: required flag(s) "scope" not set` is raised. 

```console
$ rspm create token --sources 'api-local-r' --description 'Source that contains remotely uploaded R packages'
Error: required flag(s) "scope" not set
```

We should add the `--scope` flag, presumably to `sources:write`, see https://docs.posit.co/rspm/admin/admin-cli/#api-tokens-scopes and also update the docs at https://github.com/rstudio/package-manager-demo/blob/main/python-package-manager-demo/README.md#api-token-generation and https://github.com/rstudio/package-manager-demo/blob/main/pypi-to-local-python/README.md#prerequisites

title: use setuptools for demo python package
Python package does not work when installed
description:
## Reprex

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel build
pip list
# Package         Version
# --------------- -------
# build           0.10.0
# packaging       23.1
# pip             23.1.1
# pyproject_hooks 1.0.0
# setuptools      67.7.2
# wheel           0.40.0

python -m build
pip install dist/package_manager_demo-1.0.1-py3-none-any.whl
pip list
# Package              Version
# -------------------- -------
# build                0.10.0
# package-manager-demo 1.0.1
# packaging            23.1
# pip                  23.1.1
# pyproject_hooks      1.0.0
# setuptools           67.7.2
# wheel                0.40.0

python -c 'import package_manager_demo'
# Traceback (most recent call last):
#   File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
# ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'package_manager_demo'
```

## Details

I think there are two issues:

- Additional data need to be specified in the pyproject.toml
- Rename `src/package-manager-demo` to `src/package_manager_demo`

title: Opportunities for making workflows more efficient
description:
There are a few places where we could cut out some repeated work and make the workflows more efficient:

- Each R version/distro combination is effectively building the same source package, which could also cause issues if trying to upload with the `--replace` flag (#10). You could use a matrix parameter to flag a single R version/distro combination for source package building, but it's tricky with how the matrix is done now with both R version and distro being their own variables. One way to get around that could be to `include` an additional matrix config (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-jobs/using-a-matrix-for-your-jobs#example-expanding-configurations)
- Separate jobs are created for every RSPM endpoint right now, so each source/binary package is being built 3 times even though they're the same package. Some users might want completely identical packages (i.e., same build timestamp) to be uploaded to staging/prod instances as well. We could move the RSPM endpoint/tokens out of the build matrix and into some global list that each job iterates through.

title: Consider adding example/documentation for overwriting an existing package
description:
The current workflow uploads a package version just once without ever replacing it, e.g.:
```sh
./rspm add --source=local-api --path=packageManagerDemo_1.0.0.tar.gz || echo 'Already uploaded'
```

Many users will probably want this behavior, but others may want to republish an existing version as well, using `rspm add --replace`. This should be especially common for development versions where you're updating a package without bumping its version. Some packages will bump the development version on every push to GitHub, but this is rare to see.

Since either behavior could be wanted, I'm not sure about putting both of these in the example workflows, and maybe we just document in the README that you can add `--replace` to overwrite. Or pick whatever behavior ends up being more common and use that.

Note: one caveat with using `--replace` is that there would be a lot of redundant source package uploads, since each R version/distro combination will effectively be uploading the same source package.

title: Example for building and uploading on Windows
description: It would be nice to show an example on Windows as well, since the steps will be different compared to Linux. Or possibly not, as GHA supports using bash on Linux, and the Linux commands may just work without having to write a separate PowerShell/cmd script.
